requirements: Reproduce the core contributions of ShinkaEvolve: an open-source LLM-driven evolutionary program optimization framework achieving state-of-the-art sample efficiency across circle packing, AIME agent scaffold design, ALE-Bench competitive programming, and MoE load balancing loss discovery.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ShinkaEvolve framework environment, dependencies, LLM API access, and core evolutionary loop are set up as described in Section 3, Appendix A, and Listing 1.
The ShinkaEvolve repository is installed with all required Python dependencies for running evolutionary discovery experiments.
Code has been implemented that installs the ShinkaEvolve package (importable as `shinka`) with submodules `shinka.core`, `shinka.database`, and `shinka.launch` available for import.

verification.spec: Run `pip install -e .` on the ShinkaEvolve repo, then execute `python -c 'import shinka; import shinka.core; import shinka.database; import shinka.launch'` and assert exit code 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides an `EvolutionRunner` class in `shinka.core` accepting `evo_config`, `job_config`, and `db_config` arguments and exposing a `.run()` method that starts the evolutionary loop.

verification.spec: Import `EvolutionRunner` from `shinka.core`, use `inspect.signature` to verify it accepts parameters `evo_config`, `job_config`, and `db_config`, and assert that `hasattr(EvolutionRunner, 'run')` and the `run` method is callable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides `EvolutionConfig`, `DatabaseConfig`, and `LocalJobConfig` configuration dataclasses with sensible defaults so a minimal experiment can be launched by specifying only `init_program_path` and `eval_program_path`.

verification.spec: Import `EvolutionConfig`, `DatabaseConfig`, `LocalJobConfig`. Instantiate each providing only `init_program_path` and `eval_program_path` where required; assert instantiation succeeds and all other fields have default values via `dataclasses.fields`.

sub_tasks.requirements: LLM API access is configured for the ensemble of providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek) used by ShinkaEvolve for mutation, meta-scratchpad, novelty judging, and embeddings.

Code has been implemented that supports querying LLM mutation models from at least the four leading API providers referenced in the paper: OpenAI (GPT family), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), and DeepSeek.

verification.spec: Inspect the LLM client dispatch module in shinka; assert it defines client adapters or routing for at least four provider identifiers matching OpenAI (gpt-*), Anthropic (claude-*), Google (gemini-*), and DeepSeek (deepseek-*). Verify by listing supported model prefixes in the model registry.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reads API credentials for each supported LLM provider from environment variables (or an equivalent secrets mechanism) and fails gracefully with an informative error when a required key is missing for a configured model.

verification.spec: Unset the API key env var for a configured provider (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) and attempt to instantiate the LLM client / kick off a run. Assert the framework raises a clear exception whose message names the missing env var and the affected model, rather than crashing with a low-level auth error deep in the request stack.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that samples a specific LLM together with sampling parameters (e.g., temperature or reasoning budget) from a pre-specified pool for each mutation call, with per-model temperature lists configurable (e.g., [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]).

verification.spec: Configure an LLM pool with 2+ models each having a temperatures list like [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]. Monkeypatch the LLM client to record (model_name, temperature) tuples. Trigger 30 mutation calls and assert that multiple distinct (model, temperature) pairs are observed, and each observed temperature belongs to the configured list.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports an embedding model (e.g., `text-embedding-3-small`) for the novelty rejection sampling module, callable via the same API-access layer as the mutation LLMs.

verification.spec: Locate the embedding client in shinka; assert it exposes an `embed(text)` (or similar) callable and that `text-embedding-3-small` is a valid configurable model identifier routed through the same API layer as mutation LLMs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The core three-phase evolutionary loop (parent/inspiration sampling, LLM-guided mutation with novelty rejection, execution and world feedback) is implemented as the driver of the evolution runner.

Code has been implemented that executes an outer loop for a configurable number of `generations` (e.g., 150 for Circle Packing, 75 for AIME, 50 for ALE-Bench, 30 for MoE) and terminates cleanly upon reaching the budget.

verification.spec: Run the main evolution loop with generations=5 and a stub evaluator that returns constant fitness. Assert the loop executes exactly 5 mutation-evaluation cycles, terminates without error, and writes 5 program entries to the database.

sub_tasks.requirements: The evolutionary loop, in every iteration, performs the three phases in order: (1) sample a parent and inspiration programs from the archive, (2) call an LLM to produce a mutated candidate subject to novelty rejection sampling, and (3) execute the candidate and store its fitness plus feedback in the archive.

verification.spec: Instrument the EvolutionRunner to log the order of internal phase calls. Run 3 evolutionary iterations with a stub LLM and stub evaluator. Assert the recorded call sequence per iteration is exactly [parent_sample, mutate_with_novelty_check, execute_and_store], and that after the loop the database contains 3 new programs each with a fitness score and feedback field.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports a queue-based sequential execution mode where each new LLM proposal is generated conditioned on all jobs that have completed so far and been written to the database.

verification.spec: Configure max_parallel_jobs=1 and run 3 generations. Log the archive snapshot passed as context to each LLM proposal; assert generation N's context contains program entries produced by all previous generations 0..N-1 (i.e., each proposal is conditioned on all previously completed jobs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports running multiple candidate evaluations concurrently up to a configurable `max_parallel_jobs` setting (e.g., 5 for Circle Packing, 1 for AIME/ALE-Bench).

verification.spec: Configure max_parallel_jobs=5 with a stub evaluator that sleeps 2 seconds and records concurrent-call count via a shared counter. Run 10 generations and assert the observed maximum concurrent evaluations reaches 5 (not 1) and total wall time is < 10x the sleep duration.

sub_tasks.requirements: The user-facing task interface (initial program with EVOLVE-BLOCK markers and evaluation script hook) is implemented as described in Listing 1 / Appendix A.

Code has been implemented that parses `EVOLVE-BLOCK-START` and `EVOLVE-BLOCK-END` text markers in the initial program and treats code outside these markers as immutable, rejecting or resampling any LLM proposal that modifies immutable regions.

verification.spec: Create an initial program containing text before an EVOLVE-BLOCK-START marker, mutable code inside, and text after EVOLVE-BLOCK-END. Simulate an LLM diff proposal that edits both mutable and immutable regions. Assert the framework rejects/resamples the proposal (returns error or triggers reflexion loop). Then submit a proposal editing only inside markers and assert it is accepted with immutable text byte-identical to the original.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes a `run_shinka_eval` helper (importable from `shinka.core`) which invokes a user-provided `run_experiment` function on a program path, runs it multiple times (`num_runs`), and aggregates metrics via a user-supplied `aggregate_metrics_fn`.

verification.spec: Import `run_shinka_eval` from `shinka.core` (or documented path). Invoke it with a trivial `run_experiment` returning a fixed metrics dict, num_runs=3, and a mean-aggregator; assert it returns the aggregated dict and that `run_experiment` was called exactly 3 times with the given program path.

sub_tasks.requirements: The evaluator returns an aggregated result dictionary containing at minimum a `combined_score` (float scalar fitness), a `public` metrics sub-dictionary visible to the LLM, a `private` metrics sub-dictionary hidden from the LLM, and a `text_feedback` string field.

verification.spec: Write a minimal evaluator returning the expected dict schema and run it through shinka's evaluation wrapper. Assert returned dict has keys `combined_score` (float), `public` (dict), `private` (dict), `text_feedback` (str). Additionally inspect prompt construction to confirm only `public` and `text_feedback` are included in LLM prompts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, upon receiving an invalid LLM patch (parsing failure or attempted modification of immutable code), resamples up to `max_patch_resamples` (default 3) times and feeds parsing feedback back to the LLM in a Reflexion-style prompt.

verification.spec: Mock the LLM to return an unparseable diff for the first 3 calls then a valid diff on the 4th. Configure `max_patch_resamples=3`. Assert exactly 3 resamples occur, the final attempt fails after 3 retries, and that on each retry the prompt contains parsing error feedback (Reflexion-style). Repeat with `max_patch_resamples=3` and success on the 3rd call to verify acceptance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Auxiliary framework infrastructure for logging, cost tracking, and interactive visualization is available.

Code has been implemented that persists every evaluated program (source code, fitness score, public metrics, parent lineage, and generation index) to an on-disk database that can be reloaded for later analysis or visualization.

verification.spec: Run 3 generations with a stub evaluator returning varied metrics. Locate the on-disk DB artifact (SQLite/JSON), reload it via the framework's DB reader, and assert each of the 3 program records contains: source code string, fitness score, public metrics dict, parent id(s), and generation index.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that tracks cumulative LLM API cost in US dollars across a run and exposes it for the evolution progress plots (matching the `Cumulative API Cost ($)` axis shown in Figures 5, 11, and 12).

verification.spec: Run a short evolution with a mocked LLM client that reports known token counts / prices per call. After the run, read the persisted per-generation cost trace (or DB field) and assert the cumulative-cost sequence is monotonically non-decreasing and equals the sum of expected per-call costs within a small tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides an interactive visualization tool (or export) for the program evolution tree, showing parent-child relationships between programs and highlighting the path to the best node, as depicted in Figure 5 (right).

verification.spec: Verify a visualization script/module exists (e.g., importable via `shinka.viz` or a CLI entry point) that reads the evolution database and produces an artifact (HTML/JSON/PNG) representing the program tree with nodes annotated by fitness and edges showing parent-child relationships, and with the best node's ancestral path distinguishable. Run it on a sample DB and assert the output file exists and references node/edge structure and best-path highlighting.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three key innovations of ShinkaEvolve are implemented: adaptive parent sampling, code novelty rejection sampling, and bandit-based LLM ensemble selection.

Parent and inspiration sampling strategies balance exploration and exploitation over island subpopulations, including hierarchical sampling and the four parent-selection strategies illustrated in Figure 2.

Code has been implemented that performs hierarchical sampling from the archive: first uniformly sampling an island ID, then sampling both the parent program and the inspiration programs from that same island.

verification.spec: Seed an archive with programs assigned known island IDs (e.g., 4 islands, distinguishable programs). Call the parent-and-inspiration sampler N=500 times and record the island IDs of (a) the sampled island, (b) the parent program, and (c) each inspiration. Assert the parent and all inspirations share the sampled island ID in 100% of calls, and that the sampled island ID distribution is approximately uniform (chi-square p>0.05).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, given a selected island, constructs the mutation context by sampling both random archive programs and the top-K performing programs to serve as inspiration exemplars alongside the primary parent.

verification.spec: Given a mock island with >20 programs of varied fitness and top_k=3, num_random=2, call the context-construction function 100 times. Assert each returned context includes exactly 1 primary parent + 3 programs from the top-3-by-fitness set + 2 randomly-drawn archive programs, and that the top-3 set is stable across calls while the random 2 vary.

sub_tasks.requirements: Parent selection supports multiple strategies (uniform, power-law with configurable alpha, hill-climbing, weighted) selectable via configuration such that a `parent_selection_strategy` setting switches the sampling behavior at runtime.

verification.spec: Build a synthetic archive of 20 programs with known fitness scores. For each of `parent_selection_strategy` in {'uniform','power_law','hill_climbing','weighted'}, draw 2000 parent samples. Assert: uniform produces near-uniform empirical distribution (chi-square p>0.01); hill_climbing selects the top-fitness program in >99% of draws; power_law with alpha=1 gives selection prob roughly proportional to 1/rank; weighted uses the s_i*h_i formula (see separate leaf).

sub_tasks.requirements: Power-law parent sampling is implemented that ranks programs by fitness (r_i=1 for the best) and assigns selection probability p_i = r_i^{-alpha} / sum_j r_j^{-alpha}.

verification.spec: Construct an archive of 5 programs with distinct fitnesses. Call the power-law sampler with alpha=1.0 to obtain the selection probabilities. Assert the returned probabilities match r_i^{-1}/sum_j r_j^{-1} to 1e-8 tolerance where r_i is the rank of program i (1 = best).

sub_tasks.requirements: The power-law implementation behaves correctly at the two limits: with alpha=0 the returned selection probabilities are uniform over all programs, and as alpha grows large probability mass concentrates on the top-ranked program (hill-climbing behavior).

verification.spec: With 5 programs of distinct fitnesses: (a) alpha=0 => selection probabilities are uniform (all 0.2 within 1e-8); (b) alpha=100 => probability of the top-ranked program > 0.99. Assert both conditions.

sub_tasks.requirements: Weighted parent sampling is implemented as described: compute alpha_0 = median of program fitnesses, s_i = sigmoid(lambda * (F(P_i) - alpha_0)), h_i = 1/(1+N(P_i)), w_i = s_i * h_i, and p_i = w_i / sum_j w_j.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic archive with known fitness values F_i and offspring counts N(P_i). Call the weighted sampling probability function directly and compare its returned probability vector to a hand-computed reference: alpha_0=median(F); s_i=sigmoid(lambda*(F_i-alpha_0)); h_i=1/(1+N_i); w_i=s_i*h_i; p_i=w_i/sum(w). Assert max abs difference < 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: The weighted sampling performance component s_i uses a configurable selection-pressure parameter lambda (defaulting to 10.0 as used in the paper's Circle Packing configuration) such that higher lambda sharpens the sigmoid around the median fitness.

verification.spec: Load the Circle Packing config and assert weighted-sampling lambda default equals 10.0. Then compute s_i=sigmoid(lambda*(F_i-median)) for a synthetic 10-program archive with lambda in {1.0, 10.0, 100.0} and assert the ratio of s_max/s_min grows monotonically with lambda, confirming lambda controls selection sharpness.

sub_tasks.requirements: The weighted sampling novelty component h_i = 1/(1+N(P_i)) uses each program's tracked offspring count so that programs with fewer offspring receive proportionally higher novelty weight, and the offspring counter is incremented whenever a program is chosen as a parent.

verification.spec: Set up 5 programs with varying offspring counts N in {0,1,2,3,4} and equal fitness. Verify the computed h_i equals 1/(1+N_i) for each. Then simulate a weighted-sampling call: after each parent selection assert the chosen program's offspring counter is incremented by exactly 1 in the archive.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a synthetic archive with known fitnesses and offspring counts, weighted sampling produces a probability distribution that (i) sums to 1, (ii) assigns strictly greater probability to a higher-fitness/lower-offspring program than to a lower-fitness/higher-offspring one, and (iii) reduces to the sigmoid performance term when all offspring counts are equal.

verification.spec: Build a synthetic archive. Compute weighted probabilities; assert (i) abs(sum(p)-1) < 1e-8, (ii) for program A with higher F and lower N than B, p_A > p_B, and (iii) with all N_i equal the weighted distribution equals the sigmoid-only distribution (up to normalization).

sub_tasks.requirements: The four parent-selection strategies visualized in Figure 2 (uniform alpha=0, hill-climbing alpha->inf, power-law alpha=1.0, weighted lambda=10) are all runnable end-to-end from configuration and produce sampling-probability distributions qualitatively matching the shapes shown in Figure 2 across offspring counts.

verification.spec: For each of the four configurations from Figure 2 (uniform alpha=0, power_law alpha=1.0, hill_climbing alpha->inf, weighted lambda=10) on a shared mock archive of 15 programs, run end-to-end through the ShinkaEvolve config-driven entry point and draw 5000 parent samples. Assert Pearson correlation between the empirical sampling probability vector and the Figure 2 shape (monotone-decreasing for power_law, near-flat for uniform, delta at rank 1 for hill_climbing, U-shaped-with-offspring-effect for weighted) each exceeds 0.9.

sub_tasks.requirements: Program mutation with LLM-guided edits and code novelty rejection sampling (embedding-based similarity plus optional LLM-as-a-novelty-judge) as described in Section 3.2 and Figure 3.
The mutation pipeline samples both an LLM and its sampling parameters (e.g., temperature, reasoning budget) from a pre-specified pool before generating each proposal.

verification.spec: Configure an LLM pool with >=2 models each having distinct temperature ranges. Patch the LLM client to record (model_name, temperature) per call and run 50 mutation generations. Assert both models are sampled at least once, and that the observed temperatures fall within the configured per-model ranges (not a single fixed value).

sub_tasks.requirements: Three mutation approaches are implemented and dispatched according to configurable probabilities: (1) diff-based SEARCH/REPLACE edits, (2) full program rewrites, and (3) crossover mutations that combine the parent with an additional sampled archive program.

verification.spec: Configure mutation-type probabilities {diff: 0.5, full: 0.3, crossover: 0.2}. Stub the LLM to record which prompt template is used. Run 500 mutation dispatches and assert empirical frequencies match within 5% tolerance. Additionally verify: diff prompts contain SEARCH/REPLACE instructions; full-rewrite prompts request full code; crossover prompts include TWO archive programs in context.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that parses `EVOLVE-BLOCK-START` / `EVOLVE-BLOCK-END` markers and enforces that any code outside these blocks is unchanged after a mutation, rejecting the proposal otherwise.

verification.spec: Create a source file with EVOLVE-BLOCK-START/END markers around a function body plus immutable header/footer code. Submit a mocked LLM patch that (a) modifies only the block: assert accepted; (b) modifies code outside the block: assert the framework rejects the patch (returns error or triggers resample) and the applied file matches the original outside the block.

sub_tasks.requirements: When a diff patch fails to parse or violates the immutable-block constraint, the framework resamples a new proposal and passes parsing/error feedback back into the prompt in a Reflexion-style loop, up to a configurable maximum number of resamples.

verification.spec: Stub the LLM to return an invalid diff on the first 2 calls and a valid diff on the 3rd. Set max_resamples=5. Run a single mutation and assert: the LLM was called exactly 3 times; the 2nd and 3rd prompts contain the error/parsing feedback from prior attempts (Reflexion style); the final accepted diff is the valid one. Then set max_resamples=1 with all-invalid stub and assert the mutation fails gracefully.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, for each candidate proposal, extracts the mutable portion of the program code and computes its embedding using a configured embedding model (e.g., `text-embedding-3-small`).

verification.spec: Pass a program with an EVOLVE-BLOCK region containing known code to the novelty pipeline with a mocked embedding client. Assert the client is called with the extracted mutable code (matching the EVOLVE-BLOCK contents) and not with the surrounding immutable code.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each new candidate embedding, the framework computes cosine similarity against the embeddings of all programs in the same island subpopulation and identifies the maximum similarity score.

verification.spec: Populate an island with 5 programs whose embeddings are known unit vectors. Submit a candidate whose embedding has known dot products {0.2, 0.4, 0.85, 0.5, 0.7} with the island. Call the similarity function and assert it returns max=0.85 (tol 1e-6) and that it computed cosine (not L2). Also verify only same-island embeddings are compared by adding a program to another island with dot product 0.99 and confirming max is still 0.85.
verification.paper_cite: Section 3.2 (Program Diversity via Novelty Rejection Sampling)

sub_tasks.requirements: A configurable similarity threshold eta (default 0.95 as used in the paper) is applied so that candidates with maximum island cosine similarity below the threshold are accepted without further checks, and candidates above the threshold trigger the LLM-as-novelty-judge stage.

verification.spec: Instrument the novelty pipeline to count calls to the LLM-novelty-judge. With threshold eta=0.95: feed a candidate whose max cosine similarity to island is 0.90 and assert judge is NOT called and candidate is accepted; feed one whose max similarity is 0.97 and assert judge IS called. Also verify config default of eta is 0.95.
verification.paper_cite: Section 3.2 (Program Diversity via Novelty Rejection Sampling)

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLM-as-novelty-judge step queries a configurable novelty-judge LLM with the candidate program and its nearest neighbor(s) and parses a binary novelty decision that determines acceptance or rejection.

verification.spec: Configure novelty_judge_model in the config. Stub the LLM client to return the string 'NOVEL: yes' on one call and 'NOVEL: no' on another. Trigger two candidates with similarity above threshold and assert: the correct model was called; the prompt contained both the candidate program and at least one nearest-neighbor program; the first candidate was accepted and the second rejected based on parsed decisions.

sub_tasks.requirements: When a candidate is rejected as non-novel (by either the embedding threshold followed by the LLM judge or by the judge alone), the mutation pipeline resamples a new candidate up to a configurable `max_novelty_attempts` before giving up on that generation.

verification.spec: Set max_novelty_attempts=4. Stub the LLM to always produce highly similar candidates (above threshold) and the novelty judge to always return 'not novel'. Trigger one mutation and count LLM mutation calls; assert exactly 4 attempts were made and then the generation was skipped/failed cleanly (no crash). Then flip judge to return 'novel' on attempt 3 and assert exactly 3 attempts occur and the candidate is accepted.

sub_tasks.requirements: In an end-to-end unit test, a candidate that is a near-duplicate of an existing archive program (embedding cosine > 0.95) is deterministically routed to the LLM-as-novelty-judge, and a candidate with cosine well below the threshold bypasses the judge, matching the flow shown in Figure 3.

verification.spec: End-to-end test with two candidates and mocked embedding/LLM: candidate 1 has cosine ~0.99 to archive => assert LLM-novelty-judge is called exactly once and its verdict decides acceptance; candidate 2 has cosine ~0.30 => assert judge is not called and candidate is accepted. Verify flow via call spies matches Figure 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Bandit-based adaptive LLM ensemble selection (UCB1 variant with reward transformation r_i^u) updates each LLM's sampling probability at the end of every generation as described in Section 3.3.
The framework maintains, for each LLM in the configured pool, a visitation counter and a running estimate of its expected transformed reward that are updated after each evaluated mutation.

verification.spec: Instantiate the LLM-bandit with a pool of 3 named models. Feed a sequence of (model, reward) update events and after each event inspect the bandit's per-model state; assert visitation count for each model equals the number of times it was updated and the running expected reward equals the arithmetic mean (or configured exponential moving average) of the observed transformed rewards within tolerance 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, given a mutation with raw fitness r_i, computes the baseline r_i^b as the maximum fitness between the mutation's parent program and the initial program from the database.

verification.spec: Unit test: construct a mock database with an initial program (fitness 0.5) and a parent program (fitness 0.7), then create a child mutation with fitness 0.9. Invoke the baseline computation function and assert r_i^b == max(0.7, 0.5) = 0.7. Repeat with parent fitness < initial fitness to confirm baseline == initial fitness.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reward transformation r_i^u = exp(max(r_i - r_i^b, 0)) - 1 is implemented so that non-improving mutations receive exactly 0 reward and improving mutations receive an exponentially scaled positive reward.

verification.spec: Directly invoke the bandit reward-transform function with pairs (r_i, r_i^b): assert that (r_i=5, r_b=10) -> 0.0; (r_i=10, r_b=10) -> 0.0; (r_i=11, r_b=10) -> exp(1)-1 ≈ 1.7183 (tolerance 1e-6); (r_i=12, r_b=10) -> exp(2)-1 ≈ 6.389 (tolerance 1e-4).

sub_tasks.requirements: The transformed rewards r_i^u are normalized using tracked running statistics (e.g., mean/std) over observed rewards before being used to update each LLM's estimate, ensuring invariance to the fitness scale of the target domain.

verification.spec: Unit test: feed a stream of raw r_i^u values with known mean/std (e.g., from N(10,2) distribution) into the LLM bandit reward normalizer, then feed a second stream scaled by 1000 (from N(10000,2000)). Verify that the normalized reward statistics used to update the LLM arms are approximately equal (mean ~0, std ~1) in both cases, demonstrating scale invariance.

sub_tasks.requirements: LLM selection uses a UCB1 rule that combines each model's normalized mean transformed reward with an exploration bonus proportional to sqrt(ln(total_visits) / visits_k), scaled by a configurable exploration coefficient (default 1.0 for Circle Packing).

verification.spec: Feed the bandit selector a state with known visit counts and mean rewards for two models and exploration_coef=1.0. Manually compute UCB1 = mean + 1.0*sqrt(ln(total)/visits_k) and assert the selector's internal scores match to 1e-6. Verify exploration_coef default is 1.0 in the Circle Packing config.

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLM selection strategy is configurable via a `llm_dynamic_selection` option that switches between at least three modes: single-LLM (fixed model), uniform fixed ensemble, and `ucb1` bandit-based ensemble.

verification.spec: Inspect the configuration schema (e.g., DatabaseConfig or EvolutionConfig) to confirm the presence of a `llm_dynamic_selection` field. Instantiate the evolution loop with each of the three modes ('single', 'fixed'/'uniform', 'ucb1') and verify no config validation errors and that the selected LLM sampler class differs across modes.

sub_tasks.requirements: On a deterministic synthetic bandit test where one LLM consistently produces improving mutations and another consistently produces non-improving ones, the UCB1 selector's chosen-arm frequency shifts toward the improving LLM as visits accumulate, while still selecting the weaker arm often enough to satisfy the log-visit exploration term.

verification.spec: Deterministic synthetic bandit test: create two mock LLM arms A (returns rewards ~ N(1.0, 0.1) above baseline) and B (returns rewards ~ N(-0.5, 0.1)). Run the UCB1 selector for 200 iterations updating on the mock rewards. Assert (a) arm A's selection frequency exceeds arm B's after 100 iterations, (b) arm B is still selected at least 5% of the time (exploration), (c) both arm counts monotonically increase.

sub_tasks.requirements: The bandit update is triggered once per generation at the end of that generation (not per proposal), and only completed evaluations that carry a valid fitness value contribute to the visitation counts and reward estimates.

verification.spec: Instrument the evolution loop to log bandit state updates. Run a short mock evolution with generation_size=5 and record when arm counts change. Verify: (a) arm updates occur exactly once per generation (batched), not once per proposal; (b) proposals with fitness=None (failed evaluations) do not increment visitation counters or reward estimates.

sub_tasks.requirements: Support for a heterogeneous LLM pool is implemented, including at minimum GPT (e.g., `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `o4-mini`, `gpt-5*`), Gemini (`gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash`), Claude (`claude-sonnet-4`), and DeepSeek model families, so that any subset can be enabled per task configuration.

verification.spec: Inspect the LLM client factory / registered model list and verify presence of identifiers matching each family: at least one `gpt-4.1*` or `gpt-5*` or `o4-mini`, one `gemini-2.5-*`, one `claude-sonnet-4` or `claude-*`, and one `deepseek-*`. Confirm each can be instantiated via config (no import errors) when enabled independently.

sub_tasks.requirements: The archive maintenance, island subpopulation model with migration, and the three mutation operators (diff, full-rewrite, crossover) with EVOLVE-BLOCK markers are implemented per Sections 3.1-3.2.
The program archive stores evaluated programs with fitness, metadata, and enforces an elite-size constraint.

Code has been implemented that maintains a fixed-size archive/database data structure storing each evaluated program along with its scalar fitness, public metrics, textual feedback, and metadata (e.g., parent id, island id, generation).

verification.spec: Import the archive/database class and confirm it exposes an add(program) method and stores program records with attributes: code, scalar fitness, public_metrics dict, text_feedback string, parent_id, island_id, generation. Add 3 mock programs and verify all fields round-trip via retrieval.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces an elite-size constraint on the archive so that a configurable elite fraction (e.g., 0.3 on Circle Packing) of top-performing programs is preserved when the archive is pruned.

verification.spec: Instantiate DatabaseConfig(archive_size=10, elite_selection_ratio=0.3). Insert 20 mock programs with varied fitness values. Trigger pruning and assert (a) archive contains <= 10 programs, (b) the top ceil(10 * 0.3) = 3 elites (highest fitness) are all retained.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes a DatabaseConfig accepting archive_size, elite_selection_ratio, archive_inspirations, top_k_inspirations, num_islands, migration_interval, migration_rate, island_elitism, parent_selection_strategy, and parent_selection_lambda parameters, and applies them during evolution.

verification.spec: Instantiate DatabaseConfig with all listed parameters (archive_size, elite_selection_ratio, archive_inspirations, top_k_inspirations, num_islands, migration_interval, migration_rate, island_elitism, parent_selection_strategy, parent_selection_lambda). Assert no schema/validation errors, and that each value is retrievable as an attribute on the config object.

sub_tasks.requirements: When run with archive_size=40 and elite_selection_ratio=0.3 on the Circle Packing setup, the archive maintains at most 40 stored programs and retains the specified elite fraction across generations as verified by inspection of the stored database.

verification.spec: Run the Circle Packing configuration with archive_size=40, elite_selection_ratio=0.3, for a short mock evolution injecting 100 mock evaluations. At the end, load the stored database and verify (a) total stored programs <= 40, (b) the top 12 (= floor(40*0.3)) by fitness are all present.

sub_tasks.requirements: The island subpopulation model with parallel evolution, migration, and island-best protection is implemented.

Code has been implemented that partitions the archive into a configurable number of independent island subpopulations, each seeded from the same initial program, and each program in the archive is tagged with an island id.

verification.spec: Initialize the archive with num_islands=4 and a single seed program. Immediately inspect the archive; assert 4 programs exist (one per island) with distinct island_id values in {0,1,2,3} but identical source code. After inserting 20 more mock programs (assigned to islands), verify each program's island_id is in the valid range.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that samples the island id uniformly at random for each generation and uses that island as the origin from which both the parent and inspiration programs are drawn.

verification.spec: Set num_islands=4, seed archive with programs on each island. Call the parent/inspiration sampling entry point 1000 times with a fixed RNG. Record the sampled island id and verify (a) frequencies of each island are approximately uniform (chi-square p>0.05), (b) sampled parent and inspiration programs all share the sampled island_id.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs periodic migration of programs between islands every migration_interval generations at a configurable migration_rate, copying selected programs to other islands.

verification.spec: Configure num_islands=4, migration_interval=10, migration_rate=0.2. Run 30 mock generations logging migration events. Assert (a) migration events occur only at generations 10, 20, 30 (multiples of interval), (b) at each event, approximately 20% of non-elite island members are copied to other islands.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, when island_elitism is enabled, prevents the current best-performing program of each island from migrating out, ensuring the island's top solution remains local.

verification.spec: Set island_elitism=True, seed each of 4 islands with 5 programs of distinct fitness. Trigger migration. For each island, record the best program before migration and verify it still resides in its original island after migration (i.e., was not moved out). Repeat with island_elitism=False and observe that best programs may migrate.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral test: with migration_rate=0.0 (Circle Packing config) no cross-island migration events occur, whereas with migration_rate>0 and interval=10 migrations occur at the expected cadence, as verifiable from logged migration events.

verification.spec: Run configuration A: migration_rate=0.0, num_islands=4, migration_interval=10 for 30 generations; assert zero migration events logged. Run configuration B: migration_rate=0.1, migration_interval=10 for 30 generations; assert migration events logged at generations 10, 20, 30 and non-zero programs copied at each.

sub_tasks.requirements: The mutation context construction assembles a primary parent plus inspiration programs (top-K and random archive samples) to prompt the LLM.
Code has been implemented that, given a sampled island, selects a primary parent program from that island's subpopulation using the configured parent-selection strategy.

verification.spec: Populate one island with 10 programs of known fitness. Configure parent_selection_strategy='weighted' (or 'power_law') and call the parent selection API 500 times. Verify (a) sampled parent is always from the requested island, (b) the empirical distribution over programs matches the theoretical formula for the strategy within chi-square tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that samples top_k_inspirations best-performing programs and archive_inspirations - top_k_inspirations random archive programs from the sampled island to serve as inspiration exemplars in the mutation prompt.

verification.spec: Set archive_inspirations=5, top_k_inspirations=2. Populate an island with 20 programs of distinct fitness. Call the inspiration sampler 100 times and verify each returned set contains exactly 5 programs, always including the top 2 by fitness, plus 3 random samples from the remainder.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that formats the mutation prompt to include the current parent program, its performance metrics, textual feedback, and the inspiration programs as context for the LLM.

verification.spec: Build a mutation prompt using a mock parent program (with populated metrics dict and text_feedback string) and a list of 3 inspiration programs. Inspect the resulting prompt string and assert it contains: (a) the parent's source code, (b) each performance metric key/value, (c) the text feedback string, (d) each inspiration program's code.

sub_tasks.requirements: EVOLVE-BLOCK markers delimit mutable code regions and are enforced across all mutation operators.

Code has been implemented that parses source files to identify regions delimited by the text markers `EVOLVE-BLOCK-START` and `EVOLVE-BLOCK-END`, treating code inside as mutable and code outside as immutable.

verification.spec: Create a Python source file with two EVOLVE-BLOCK-START/END regions interspersed with immutable code. Call the parser and verify (a) it identifies exactly two mutable regions with correct start/end line numbers, (b) the extracted mutable text matches the content between markers, (c) code outside markers is classified as immutable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after any mutation, validates that immutable regions outside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers are byte-identical to the parent's immutable regions and rejects the proposal otherwise.

verification.spec: Create a parent source with a single EVOLVE-BLOCK region. Produce three mutated candidates: (1) valid change only inside the block, (2) change to a line outside the block, (3) change to both. Feed each to the immutability validator; assert (1) passes, (2) and (3) are rejected with an error indicating immutable-code violation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, on invalid patches (immutable code touched or unparseable diff), resamples the LLM proposal up to max_patch_resamples/max_patch_attempts times and provides parsing feedback to the LLM using a Reflexion-style loop.

verification.spec: Mock the LLM to return invalid patches (touches immutable region) for the first 2 calls and a valid patch on the 3rd. Set max_patch_resamples=3. Invoke the mutation pipeline and verify (a) 3 LLM calls occur, (b) the 2 intermediate failures are appended as Reflexion-style feedback in the retry prompts, (c) the final valid patch is applied. Then set max_patch_resamples=1 and confirm the pipeline gives up after 1 retry.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three mutation operators (diff-based edits, full rewrites, crossover) are implemented and stochastically dispatched.

Code has been implemented that supports a configurable list of patch_types = [diff, full, cross] with associated categorical sampling probabilities patch_type_probs, so each generation the mutation operator is drawn accordingly.

verification.spec: Load a config with patch_types=['diff','full','cross'] and patch_type_probs=[0.5,0.3,0.2]. Instantiate the mutation operator dispatcher and confirm (a) it accepts all three operator names without error, (b) exposes a sample_patch_type() method that returns one of the three strings, (c) validates that probabilities sum to 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral test: over a large number of sampled mutations with patch_type_probs=[0.45, 0.45, 0.1] (Circle Packing) or [0.6, 0.3, 0.1] (AIME/ALE) the empirical operator frequencies approximately match the specified distribution.

verification.spec: For each configuration, call sample_patch_type() 10000 times with a fixed RNG. Config A patch_type_probs=[0.45,0.45,0.1]: assert empirical frequencies for diff, full, cross are within 0.02 of (0.45, 0.45, 0.10). Config B [0.6,0.3,0.1]: assert empirical frequencies within 0.02 of (0.60, 0.30, 0.10).

sub_tasks.requirements: The diff-based edit operator is implemented following AlphaEvolve's SEARCH/REPLACE block format, parsing LLM output into SEARCH and REPLACE sections and applying targeted substitutions to the parent program.

verification.spec:
Craft an LLM output string containing two AlphaEvolve-style SEARCH/REPLACE blocks (e.g., '<<<<<<< SEARCH
foo
=======
bar
>>>>>>> REPLACE'). Feed to the diff parser with a parent source containing 'foo'. Verify (a) both blocks are parsed into (search,replace) tuples, (b) applying them yields a program with 'foo' substituted by 'bar' at the correct locations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that rejects diff proposals whose SEARCH block fails to match the parent source verbatim or whose applied REPLACE would modify code outside EVOLVE-BLOCK regions.

verification.spec: Case 1: parent source lacks the text specified in SEARCH block -> diff application returns an error indicating no verbatim match; parent source unchanged. Case 2: SEARCH matches a line outside any EVOLVE-BLOCK region -> diff application rejected with immutable-region violation. Case 3: SEARCH matches text inside EVOLVE-BLOCK -> accepted and applied.

sub_tasks.requirements: The full-rewrite operator is implemented so the LLM produces a complete replacement program while the framework programmatically re-inserts the parent's non-mutable code, guaranteeing immutable blocks are preserved.

verification.spec: Inspect the mutation module for a full-rewrite operator implementation. Verify that after the LLM returns a full replacement program, the framework parses EVOLVE-BLOCK-START/EVOLVE-BLOCK-END markers and programmatically re-inserts the parent's immutable code regions. Construct a parent program with immutable and mutable blocks, invoke the full-rewrite operator with a mocked LLM that alters immutable content, and confirm the resulting program's immutable regions match the parent's exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The crossover mutation operator is implemented such that an additional archive program is sampled and the LLM is prompted to combine the parent and that secondary program into a new offspring while respecting EVOLVE-BLOCK boundaries.

verification.spec: Trigger the crossover operator with a mocked LLM. Assert (1) two archive programs are sampled (parent + secondary) and both appear in the constructed prompt, (2) the operator's output preserves immutable regions from the parent (verified by diffing outside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers).

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral test: for each of the three operators, a produced offspring can be applied to the parent and yields a program whose immutable regions equal the parent's immutable regions and whose mutable regions differ.

verification.spec: For each of the three mutation operators (diff-based, full-rewrite, crossover), construct a parent program with clearly marked immutable and mutable EVOLVE-BLOCK regions and invoke the operator with a mocked LLM that proposes changes. Assert (a) the offspring's immutable regions are byte-identical to the parent's, and (b) the offspring's mutable regions differ from the parent's.

sub_tasks.requirements: Parent selection strategies (power-law, uniform, hill-climbing, weighted) are implemented per Section 3.1.

Code has been implemented that supports a power-law parent sampling strategy where programs are ranked by fitness (r_i=1 best) and selected with probability p_i = r_i^{-alpha} / sum_j r_j^{-alpha}, with alpha configurable.

verification.spec: Locate the power-law parent sampling implementation. Populate an archive with N programs of known distinct fitnesses, set alpha to a specific value (e.g., 1.0), and draw a large number of samples (>=10000). Empirically verify that the sampling frequencies match p_i = r_i^{-alpha} / sum_j r_j^{-alpha} within chi-squared tolerance. Confirm alpha is exposed as a configuration option.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that setting alpha=0 in the power-law strategy yields uniform sampling and alpha->infinity yields deterministic hill-climbing (always the top-ranked program), verifiable via unit-level probability checks.

verification.spec: With the power-law sampler and an archive of at least 5 distinct-fitness programs: (1) set alpha=0 and verify that the theoretical selection probability of each program equals 1/N (all uniform); (2) set alpha to a very large value (e.g., 1e6) and verify that the sampler deterministically returns the top-ranked (rank=1) program across many draws.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the weighted parent sampling strategy that, given fitnesses {F(P_i)} and offspring counts {N(P_i)}, computes median fitness alpha_0, performance scores s_i = sigmoid(lambda*(F(P_i)-alpha_0)), novelty scores h_i = 1/(1+N(P_i)), and probabilities p_i = (s_i * h_i)/sum_j(s_j * h_j).

verification.spec: Locate the weighted parent sampling implementation. Construct a hand-designed archive with known fitnesses and offspring counts, compute the expected values of alpha_0 = median(F), s_i = sigmoid(lambda * (F(P_i) - alpha_0)), h_i = 1/(1 + N(P_i)), and p_i = (s_i * h_i) / sum_j(s_j * h_j). Call the sampler's probability-computing function and assert the returned probabilities match the closed form within 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral test: with parent_selection_strategy=weighted and lambda=10.0, the implementation reproduces the sigmoid-scaled probabilities in a controlled unit test (given hand-set fitnesses and offspring counts, computed p_i matches the closed-form formula to numerical precision).

verification.spec: Instantiate the weighted parent sampler with parent_selection_strategy='weighted' and lambda=10.0. Feed an archive with hand-set fitnesses F=[0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.3, 0.7] and offspring counts N=[0, 2, 1, 5, 3]. Compute the expected p_i from the closed-form formula. Compare against the implementation's output; assert element-wise absolute difference < 1e-6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that tracks and updates the offspring count N(P_i) for every parent whenever a new child program is produced from it, and this count feeds directly into the weighted sampling novelty term.

verification.spec: Instantiate the archive and produce K child programs from a specific parent P via the framework's mutation pipeline (mocking the LLM). After each child is added, query the parent's offspring counter N(P) and verify it has incremented by 1. Then invoke the weighted sampler's novelty term computation and confirm h_i = 1/(1+N(P)) matches for that parent.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports a Best-of-N baseline strategy (always sample the initial program as parent, ignoring history) so it can be selected via configuration for ablation runs.

verification.spec: Set parent_selection_strategy='best_of_n' (or equivalent) in configuration and run 5 generations. Log the parent program ID used for each mutation; assert every mutation uses the initial seed program as its parent (offspring lineage all point to program 0).

sub_tasks.requirements: The meta-scratchpad system for periodic summarization, textual feedback, multi-objective public/private metrics, and the UCB1-based adaptive LLM sampling with the modified reward transform are implemented.
Multi-objective assessment with public/private metrics, textual feedback, and combined_score is implemented and stored in the archive.

Code has been implemented so that the evaluator (run_shinka_eval) returns a dictionary containing `combined_score` (scalar fitness), `public` metrics (visible to the LLM prompts), `private` metrics (not exposed to LLM prompts), `extra_data` (stored as pickle), and `text_feedback` (string feedback), matching the API shown in Appendix A.

verification.spec: Import the evaluator entry point (run_shinka_eval or equivalent) and call it on a minimal example task. Assert the returned object is a dict containing the keys: 'combined_score' (scalar float), 'public' (dict), 'private' (dict), 'extra_data' (picklable object), and 'text_feedback' (str). Verify extra_data round-trips through pickle.dumps/pickle.loads.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that after program execution the archive stores the scalar fitness r_i, the set of exposed public metrics, and the textual feedback for each program, enabling downstream retrieval when constructing mutation prompts.

verification.spec: Run a mini evolution loop of 3-5 generations on a toy task. After execution, iterate over archive entries and confirm each stored program record contains the scalar fitness r_i, the public metrics dict, and the text_feedback string. Then retrieve one entry and confirm these fields are accessible for downstream prompt construction.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that private metrics are strictly withheld from prompts constructed for the mutation LLM, novelty judge LLM, and meta-scratchpad LLM, while public metrics and text_feedback are exposed.

verification.spec: Create an archive entry with public metrics {'acc': 0.9} and private metrics containing a unique sentinel string 'PRIVATE_SENTINEL_XYZ'. Invoke the three prompt-construction paths (mutation prompt, novelty judge prompt, meta-scratchpad prompt) on this entry. Assert none of the rendered prompts contain 'PRIVATE_SENTINEL_XYZ', but that public metrics and text_feedback strings do appear in the mutation prompt.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the mutation prompt template embeds the current program's `performance_metrics` and a `text_feedback_section` block in the format shown in Section 3.3 (`# Current program` header, code block, performance metrics, textual feedback, `# Instructions`, `# Task`).

verification.spec: Render the diff-edit mutation prompt with a sample program and metrics. Assert the rendered string contains, in order, the header '# Current program', a fenced code block with the program body, the phrase 'performance metrics of the program:' followed by the metrics, an optional text_feedback_section block, then '# Instructions' and '# Task' sections, matching the template shown in Section 3.3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a candidate program is evaluated over multiple independent runs (num_runs), the per-run results are aggregated via a user-provided `aggregate_metrics_fn` into the final combined_score/public/private/text_feedback structure.

verification.spec: Configure num_runs=3 and provide a custom aggregate_metrics_fn that produces deterministic outputs (e.g., mean of per-run fitness). Run the evaluator on a program producing known per-run values [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]. Verify the final returned combined_score equals aggregate_metrics_fn's output (2.0), and that public/private/text_feedback are populated by the same aggregation function's return value.

sub_tasks.requirements: UCB1-based adaptive LLM ensemble sampling with the ShinkaEvolve-specific reward transform is implemented.

Code has been implemented so that each LLM in the configured ensemble maintains a visitation counter n_k and an estimate of its expected transformed reward, updated after every generation using the outcomes of that LLM's sampled mutations.

verification.spec: Configure an ensemble of 3 LLMs and run 6 mock generations where each LLM is selected in turn and produces a mutation with a known reward. After the loop, access the sampler's internal state and assert each LLM has visitation_count == 2 and mean_reward equal to the mean of its assigned rewards (within 1e-6).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the LLM sampling probability at each generation is derived from UCB1 scores of the form mean_reward_k + c * sqrt(ln(N)/n_k), configurable via `LLM dynamic selection = ucb1` and an exploration coefficient (e.g., 1.0 as used for Circle Packing).

verification.spec: Set LLM_dynamic_selection='ucb1' and exploration coefficient c=1.0. Populate the bandit with known visitation counts n_k and mean rewards. Query the sampler's UCB1 score computation and assert score_k = mean_reward_k + c * sqrt(ln(N)/n_k) for each arm within 1e-6. Confirm c is configurable and defaults appropriately for Circle Packing.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that for each new program i the baseline reward r_i^b is computed as max(fitness(parent_i), fitness(initial_program)) using the stored archive entries.

verification.spec: Seed the archive with an initial program (fitness=0.3) and a parent program (fitness=0.7). Produce a child from the parent and call the reward-transformation function. Assert that the baseline r_i^b used equals max(0.7, 0.3) = 0.7. Repeat with parent fitness=0.1 and confirm r_i^b = 0.3 (the initial program).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the transformed reward used to update the LLM bandit is r_i^u = exp(max(r_i - r_i^b, 0)) - 1, exactly matching the formula in Section 3.3 that promotes high-risk, high-reward improvements over safe minor edits.

verification.spec: Instrument the bandit update path. Inject a mutation with r_i=2.0 and r_i^b=1.5 and confirm the reward passed into the bandit update equals exp(0.5)-1 ≈ 0.6487 (within 1e-6). Also test r_i=1.0, r_i^b=1.5 => reward 0.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the transformed rewards r_i^u are normalized using running statistics (e.g., running mean/std) over observed rewards to provide fitness-scale invariance across different domains before being fed to the UCB1 update.

verification.spec: Instantiate the LLM-bandit component and feed a synthetic stream of transformed rewards r_i^u with widely different scales (e.g., first batch ~1e-3, second batch ~1e3). Verify that the values used in the UCB update are normalized (e.g., z-scored or divided by running std) rather than raw, by asserting update magnitudes differ from raw values and match a running-statistics normalization within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a new mutation is sampled the choice of LLM is drawn according to the current UCB1-derived distribution, and the associated LLM identifier is recorded with the program so its outcome can update the correct arm.

verification.spec: Fix the UCB1 sampler's random seed so LLM selection is deterministic. Run the mutation pipeline once and record which LLM was chosen. Inspect the resulting program's stored metadata and assert it contains the correct LLM identifier. Then trigger an outcome update and verify the bandit statistics for the recorded LLM (and only that LLM) have changed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a scripted archive where LLM A produces mutations with r_i - r_i^b = 1.0 and LLM B produces mutations with r_i - r_i^b <= 0, the bandit's mean estimate for A must equal exp(1) - 1 (≈1.7183) up to normalization and for B must equal 0 before normalization.

verification.spec: Script an archive where mutations from LLM A always give r_i-r_i^b=1.0 and LLM B always give <=0. After feeding these into the bandit's update method, inspect the internal per-model reward sums/means: A's per-sample transformed reward equals exp(1)-1 (≈1.7183) and B's equals 0, before any normalization step.

sub_tasks.requirements: The meta-scratchpad system that periodically summarizes recent programs into insights and recommendations appended to mutation prompts is implemented.

Code has been implemented so that every T generations (configured by `meta_recommendation_interval`, e.g., 10 for Circle Packing, 5 for ALE-Bench) a meta-scratchpad update is triggered that collects recent program evaluations from the archive.

verification.spec: Set meta_recommendation_interval=10 and run 25 mock generations while patching the meta-scratchpad LLM call to log invocations. Assert the meta-scratchpad update was triggered at generations 10 and 20 (and not at intermediate generations). Verify that each triggered update received recent archive entries as input.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that a dedicated meta-agent LLM (configured via `meta_models`, e.g., gpt-5-nano / gpt-4.1 / gpt-5-mini) is queried with recent program summaries to produce (i) individual program summaries, (ii) global insights across programs, and (iii) actionable implementation recommendations, matching Figure 4.

verification.spec: Configure `meta_models` to a mocked LLM and set the meta-scratchpad interval T=5. Run 10 iterations of the evolutionary loop with dummy programs and evaluations. Assert the meta-agent LLM is called at least twice (at generation 5 and 10), that its input contains recent program summaries, and that its output is parsed into three sections (per-program summaries, global insights, implementation recommendations) which are appended to subsequent mutation prompts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the number of recommendations retained is capped by `max_meta_recommendations` (e.g., 5), and older recommendations are pruned or replaced when the cap is exceeded.

verification.spec: Set max_meta_recommendations=5. Inject 8 recommendations sequentially into the meta-scratchpad store via repeated meta-update calls. After each insertion beyond the cap, assert the stored recommendation list length is <= 5, and confirm that older entries are pruned or replaced (e.g., FIFO or oldest-out policy).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the current meta-scratchpad (insights + recommendations) is appended to the mutation prompt sent to the mutation LLM in subsequent generations, providing high-level guidance from accumulated evolutionary experience.

verification.spec: Run a short evolution (e.g., 15 generations) with meta-scratchpad enabled. Intercept or log the mutation prompt strings sent to the mutation LLM after the first scratchpad refresh; assert the prompt contains the scratchpad's insights/recommendations text (identifiable by a known header substring or by matching the string returned from the meta-agent).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the meta-scratchpad LLM is called with the temperature specified in `meta_temperatures` (e.g., 0.0) and the meta-scratchpad content is persisted so it can be inspected and reused across the run.

verification.spec: Configure meta_temperatures=[0.0]. Patch the LLM client so it records the temperature it was called with. Trigger a meta-scratchpad update and assert the recorded temperature is 0.0. Then inspect the persisted meta-scratchpad file/state and confirm its contents are readable and reused (embedded in the next mutation prompt).

sub_tasks.requirements: Given a run configured with meta_recommendation_interval = 10 and 30 total generations, exactly 3 meta-scratchpad refresh calls to the meta LLM must occur, and the mutation prompt at generation 15 must contain the recommendations produced at the generation-10 refresh.

verification.spec: Configure a run with meta_recommendation_interval=10 and generations=30 using a mocked meta LLM that returns a unique string per invocation. Assert the meta LLM is called exactly 3 times (at generations 10, 20, 30) and that the mutation prompt captured at generation 15 contains the unique string returned by the generation-10 call.

sub_tasks.requirements: The n=26 circle packing task is set up, ShinkaEvolve is run with the specified hyperparameters, and the discovered solution matches or exceeds the AlphaEvolve baseline within ~150 evaluations.
The circle packing problem is correctly formalized as a program-evolution task with proper objective, constraints, and evaluation harness.
Task definition and constraints are implemented.
Code has been implemented that sets the number of circles to n=26 to be packed within a unit square [0,1] x [0,1].

verification.spec: Load the circle-packing task configuration/initial program and assert that the number of circles constant n equals 26 and that the unit square domain corresponds to [0,1] x [0,1] (both x and y coordinate bounds).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so the objective function computes the sum of the 26 circle radii as the quantity to be maximized.

verification.spec: Call the circle-packing objective function on a hand-crafted configuration of 26 circles with known radii r_1..r_26 (all satisfying constraints). Verify the returned objective equals sum(r_i) within 1e-9.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the non-overlap constraint between every pair of circles (distance between centers >= sum of radii).

verification.spec: Construct two test configurations: (a) 26 clearly non-overlapping circles with pairwise center distance > r_i + r_j + margin; (b) a configuration with one pair of circles that overlaps by 0.01. Feed both to the constraint-checking function. Assert (a) passes the non-overlap check and (b) fails (or is penalized).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces containment of each circle inside the unit square (center coordinates within [r, 1-r] for radius r).

verification.spec: Construct (a) a configuration where every circle satisfies r <= x <= 1-r and r <= y <= 1-r, and (b) a configuration where one circle protrudes beyond the unit square (e.g., x = 0.1 with r = 0.2). Assert containment check passes on (a) and fails/penalizes (b).

sub_tasks.requirements: Verification and scoring code correctly evaluates candidate solutions.
Code has been implemented following the OpenEvolve-style verification script that permits a numerical slack of 1e-6 when checking overlap/containment constraints during the main evolution run.

verification.spec: Construct a configuration with an overlap of exactly 5e-7 between two circles and another with overlap of 1e-5. Pass both through the OpenEvolve-style verification routine used during evolution. Assert the first (5e-7 < 1e-6 slack) passes and the second (1e-5 > 1e-6 slack) fails. Repeat for containment slack.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reports the fitness of a candidate as the sum of radii when constraints are satisfied and rejects/penalizes infeasible solutions.

verification.spec: Evaluate the fitness function on: (a) a feasible 26-circle configuration and confirm the returned fitness equals sum of radii; (b) an infeasible configuration (with overlap beyond slack). Assert the infeasible case is rejected (e.g., returns None/error status) or penalized with a fitness strictly lower than any feasible sum-of-radii value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that additionally allows validating any evolved solution against the AlphaEvolve exact (no-slack) verifier for post-processing.

verification.spec: Import the circle packing validator module and invoke it on a known valid packing (26 non-overlapping circles inside unit square) and a known invalid one (with overlap or out-of-bounds circle). Assert the exact no-slack verifier returns valid for the first and invalid for the second, with no numerical tolerance/slack applied.

sub_tasks.requirements: The initial seed program and evolution scaffolding required by ShinkaEvolve are provided.
An initial program (initial.py) containing a naive circle packing solver is provided as the evolutionary seed for all islands.

verification.spec: Assert that examples/circle_packing/initial.py (or equivalent seed file path) exists, is importable, and contains a solver function that produces a valid packing of 26 circles in the unit square when executed.

sub_tasks.requirements: The initial program uses EVOLVE-BLOCK-START / EVOLVE-BLOCK-END markers to delimit the mutable region containing the packing algorithm.
